patches.old: For positive δ, decreasing δ restricts the admissible covers and therefore increases their infimum. All costs are nonnegative. If H^s(A)=0, every scale infimum is zero. By the defining greatest-lower-bound property, for every positive threshold a cover has cost below it: otherwise that positive threshold would be a lower bound. If H^s(A)=∞, its defining supremum supplies a scale with content>L for every finite L>0. Replacing that scale by its minimum with δ0 preserves this strict inequality and gives a scale no larger than δ0. These are implications for arbitrary positive L,δ0,δ. Discharge L1 and universally quantify k,A,s with its positivity condition, obtaining N001.

patches.old: For each positive s and δ in F002, choose its finite subcover T. Each ball's s-cost is≤δ^s, so the finite cost sum is finite. The infimum H^s_δ(E) is no greater than that cost, and is therefore finite. This proves the universally quantified finite-cover and content clauses in N002.

patches.old: First assume L1: n≥1. For 0<h≤1 partition each coordinate interval [−R,R] into at most ceil(2R/h) closed subintervals of length≤h. Their products cover the box and hence E. The number of cubes (possibly shorter at the boundary) is≤(2R/h+1)^n≤C h^(−n), where C=(2R+1)^n depends only on the fixed box. Each diameter is≤√n h by summing the squared coordinate differences. For s>n the total s-cost is≤C n^(s/2) h^(s−n), which tends to zero as h↓0 since s−n>0. For any fixed target scale, h can be arbitrarily small while √n h is below it; hence every scale content is zero and H^s(E)=0. N001 gives D≤s for every s>n. It follows that D≤n: if D>n, choose a finite real s strictly between n and D (also possible if D=∞), contradicting D≤s. Discharge L1. In the remaining case L2: n=0, Eucl(0) has only the empty vector; H001 implies E=Eucl(0). Its singleton cover has zero s-cost for every s>0, so N001 gives D≤s for every positive s, whence D=0. Discharge L2. Nonnegativity in both cases is N001, giving 0≤D≤n and all the remaining clauses of N002.

patches.old: Define J=(inf B−η/2,sup B+η/2). Every element of B lies between inf B and sup B, and η>0 makes both endpoint containments strict. The interval is nonempty, open and bounded. Its length is sup B−inf B+η≤ρ+η by F001. Discharge L1 and quantify B,ρ,η to obtain precisely N003. This argument invokes only the usual least-upper-bound and greatest-lower-bound properties of real numbers; it asserts no measurability of B.

patches.old: By N002, D is finite. In the n≥1 case, F004 gives dim_H(F)≤q+1 for every q>D. One such q first makes dim_H(F) finite. If dim_H(F)>D+1, a q strictly between D and dim_H(F)−1 contradicts that inequality; hence dim_H(F)≤D+1. This is the limit q↓D without assuming a measure statement at the critical exponent. The other case is F001, and n is either zero or at least one. F001 and F004 supply the more precise zero statements in their respective cases. Thus N004 follows in full.

Otherwise this sum and c are finite real numbers by F001; F003 for every ε>0 then gives c≤∑_{i∈K}ρ_i^(s+1), since a strict positive difference would be contradicted by choosing a smaller ε. Empty members have zero cost, so this is the cost of the original arbitrary V. Taking the infimum over all admissible δ-covers of F gives H^s_δ(E)≤H^(s+1)_δ(F). Discharge L1 and quantify s,δ over their positive ranges. This is N005, with no measurability premise on the covers or their projections.

patches.old: Fix k,A,e and assume L2: e(I)⊆A and dist(e(t),e(u))=|t−u| for all t,u∈I. For any countable δ-cover V of A at any positive δ, put P_i={t∈I:e(t)∈V_i}. These sets cover I. By distance preservation, every pair of points in P_i has distance at most diam(V_i), so diam(P_i)≤diam(V_i)≤δ. Therefore for every s>0, H^s_δ(I)≤∑_i diam(P_i)^s≤∑_i diam(V_i)^s. Taking the infimum over V gives H^s_δ(I)≤H^s_δ(A). This proof works for every positive s,δ and does not require any cover measurable. Taking suprema gives H^s(I)≤H^s(A). For 0<s<1, F003 therefore gives H^s(A)=∞ and N001 gives dim_H(A)≥s; the strict-between argument yields dim_H(A)≥1. Discharge L2 and quantify k,A,e, proving the complete embedding clause and finishing N006.
